(NBA). Born in the United States, he played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. After earning [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors as a sophomore in 2013–14, he declared for the [[2014 NBA draft]] and was selected in the first round with the 30th overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Nicknamed "'''Slow Mo'''", Anderson developed the ball-handling skills of a [[point guard]] at an early age, but his height provided him the versatility to play as a [[forward (basketball)|forward]]. As a high school player in [[New Jersey]], Anderson led his teams to two consecutive state titles, and was named state player of the year during his senior year. One of the top recruits out of high school, Anderson was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a freshman at UCLA while playing mostly at forward. The following season, he moved to point guard, and was voted the Most Outstanding Player of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] as the Bruins won their first conference tournament title in six years. He played four seasons with San Antonio before signing with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2018. After four seasons with the Grizzlies, he signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Anderson has also played for the [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Utah Jazz]], and [[Miami Heat]]. In 2023, Anderson became a [[naturalized]] Chinese citizen and played for [[China men's national basketball team|their national team]] in the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. ==Early life== Anderson was born on September 20, 1993, in [[New York City]], and grew up in [[Fairview, Bergen County, New Jersey|Fairview]].{{cite news |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |title=Anderson is head and shoulders above |date=July 23, 2009 |work=sny.tv |url=http://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090723&content_id=6018414&vkey=45 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029063144/http://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090723&content_id=6018414&vkey=45 |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all |access-date=October 29, 2014|quote='A lot of schools are coming at me, but I haven't looked into any of them,' said Anderson, who lives in North Bergen, N.J. and competes for the Playaz Basketball Club AAU program. "I'm still neutral."}} He attended his first basketball camp at the age of three. Anderson's father, who played basketball at Glassboro State College (now [[Rowan University]]) and became a longtime high school coach in New Jersey, groomed him to be a [[point guard]]. Although Anderson was tall, his father did not want him to be "pigeonholed" as a [[post (basketball)|post]] player.{{cite news |last=Foster |first=Chris |title=UCLA's Kyle Anderson doesn't lack confidence or intensity |date=March 12, 2014 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/college/ucla/la-sp-ucla-kyle-anderson-20140313,0,6102973,full.story#axzz2wAciTPAt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140424190445/https://www.latimes.com/sports/college/ucla/la-sp-ucla-kyle-anderson-20140313,0,6102973,full.story|archive-date=April 24, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all |access-date=March 17, 2014 }} He had his son play with older players on [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) teams; usually the smallest player on the court, Anderson developed point guard skills early while passing to his larger teammates.{{cite news|last=Parker |first=Brandon |title=St. Anthony's Kyle Anderson takes winning to a different level |date=November 14, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/high-school/new-jersey/post/_/id/486/st-anthonys-kyle-anderson-takes-winning-to-a-different-level |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140227144134/http://espn.go.com/blog/high-school/new-jersey/post/_/id/486/st-anthonys-kyle-anderson-takes-winning-to-a-different-level |archive-date=February 27, 2014 |url-status=live }} He began his high school career at [[Paterson Catholic High School]]. Although he possessed the skills of a point guard, his {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|adj=on}} height led coaches to play him on the wing or in the post. After two years at Paterson Catholic, the school closed, and Anderson moved to [[St. Anthony High School (New Jersey)|St. Anthony High School]]. Overall, he compiled 119–6 record as a four-year starter, including 65–0 in his two years at St. Anthony. When St. Anthony captured its second straight [[Tournament of Champions (NJSIAA)|New Jersey Tournament of champions]] title and concluded its second straight undefeated season with a 66–62 victory over Plainfield, Anderson was the team's third-leading scorer with 14 [[point (basketball)|points]]. Still, St. Anthony coach [[Bob Hurley]] said Anderson was the team's "heart and soul and he was the reason we won the game.’’{{cite news|url=http://www.nj.com/hssports/blog/boysbasketball/index.ssf/2012/04/kyle_anderson_of_st_anthony_is_the_star-ledgers_state_boys_basketball_player_of_the_year_for_2011-12.html|title=Kyle Anderson of St. Anthony is The Star-Ledger's state boys basketball Player of the Year for 2011–12|newspaper=The Star-Ledger|access-date=September 16, 2012|date=April 1, 2013|first=John|last=Haley}} For the season, Anderson led the team in scoring (14.7 points per game), [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] (6.5 per game), [[assist (basketball)|assists]] (3.9 per game), [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]] (2.0 per game) and deflections. ''[[The Star-Ledger]]'' named him their state boys basketball Player of the Year. He received national recognition as a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]], and he was invited to play in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. In spite of all the praise he had received in his career, Anderson was described by Hurley as "unassuming", which the coach credited to Anderson's family doing a "great job keeping him balanced." He signed a four-year deal with the [[Memphis Grizzlies|Grizzlies]] worth $37.2 million after the Spurs declined to match the offer sheet.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/07/06/report-kyle-anderson-signs-offer-sheet-memphis-grizzlies|title=Report: Kyle Anderson signs four-year offer sheet with Memphis Grizzlies|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-kyle-anderson-to-multi-year-contract-180709|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Kyle Anderson to multi-year contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}} Popovich said the figure was "beyond the pale for us", but he was happy for Anderson.
